newsitem.title: USA: California refining margins reviving - analysts.
newsitem.headline: California refining margins reviving - analysts.

text.p: California refineries have seen profits for gasoline improve in late July in the wake of brief refinery stoppages and increased exports, analysts said Wednesday.
Refineries on average earned $4.74 on a barrel of oil this week, a 25 percent improvement from two weeks ago, according to a report to clients Wednesday by Salomon Brothers oil analyst Paul Ting.
"This is well above the May level and the June level," Ting said.

On the supply side, brief production problems at Shell Oil Co's Martinez, California refinery and Exxon's Benecia plant have lifted prices 10 percent since mid-July to 69 cents a gallon, Wednesday, according to traders.
The problems ended a flawless second quarter performance for the industry, which saw plants operating at a capacity of about 95 percent, compared to 87 percent a year ago.

High volumes of supply dropped the spot price of CARB (California Air Resources Board specifications) unleaded gasoline to 55 cents a gallon in mid-June, down nearly 30 cents a gallon from late March.
"It was a combination of imports and very strong refinery production of gasoline," said Philip Tendler, analyst for Schroder Wertheim & Co in California.

The price collapse focused West Coast traders on exporting more conventional gasoline to the U.S. Gulf, which held a roughly seven-cent premium earlier this summer, traders said. About two million barrels of product, or 10 cargoes have left the West Coast since late May.

Prompt conventional unleaded gasoline in the Gulf and West Coast traded at the same level of 63 to 64 cents a gallon on Wednesday, an indication that prices are resuming their normal relationship, analysts said.
